title: Wine Club Pickup: Add Your Orders to a Napa or Sonoma Trip
description: Collecting winery orders or wine-club releases? Confirm readiness, pickup windows, the collector and packed cases before adding Napa or Sonoma stops.
cta: Build the ride around confirmed winery handoffs.
image_alt: Two plain closed cardboard cartons on a wooden counter beside an open doorway overlooking autumn vines.
body:
To collect a wine-club release or an order during a Napa or Sonoma trip, confirm with each winery that the wine is being held for pickup, is ready for your visit and can be released to the person who will attend. Then add the collection address, agreed window and packed case count to the transportation plan. A tasting appointment and a wine-order pickup are separate arrangements.

This guide is about collecting purchases already made or allocated, including orders from different dates. For deciding how to take bottles on a flight afterward, use our separate flying-home-with-wine guide.

Check the order before building the route

Find the current winery confirmation for each order. An older will-call preference is not enough to establish that this release is still at the winery: the order may have a collection deadline, a different fulfillment address or a shipping instruction.

  • Identity: purchaser or member name and the order/release reference.
  • Status: paid and ready, awaiting confirmation, already shipped, or another status the winery supplies.
  • Place: exact collection address and entrance, not just the estate name.
  • Window: permitted day/hours, any appointment requirement and the last collection date.
  • Collector: who will attend, what identification or authorization is needed and whether that person must sign.
  • Load: bottle count, number of packed cartons and approximate dimensions or unusual formats.

Ask the winery to acknowledge any change from shipping to pickup before you change the ride. Do not assume an order can be stopped after dispatch or that adding a stop brings a delivery back to the estate.

Real examples show why the confirmation matters

These are property-specific examples from the wineries' published information, checked November 18, 2026. Your current release notice and the winery's reply should settle the details for your order.

  • Stag's Leap Wine Cellars says membership defaults to shipping, with a 30-day winery pickup window if a member requests collection before the release is shipped. A planned Napa visit is therefore not itself a pickup instruction.
  • Frog's Leap describes a 30-day hold after billing for Will Call Fellow Shipments, followed by shipping with charges if uncollected. Check the billing date, rather than counting from when you happen to see the email.
  • For a Sonoma County example, Jordan's order information says website or phone orders can be collected during regular business hours once the order confirmation is received, with a signed acknowledgment when the wine changes possession. That does not establish a tasting reservation.

Do not generalize one winery's window, release procedure or shipping terms to another. If your travel dates miss the collection window, ask the winery about its available arrangements before committing to a detour.

Give every collection stop its own purpose

Separate a pickup-only visit from a tasting, tour or meal. Ask the winery whether collection uses the same entrance and whether it can be combined with your existing appointment. Our tasting and transportation checklist explains why the two confirmations need to agree.

Illustrative plan: one order is ready at a Napa winery during your confirmed visit window, while another is held in Sonoma County. First confirm both handoffs. Ask the transportation provider to review the actual route and service time, including your other appointments. If the second stop does not fit, resolve its collection or shipping arrangement with that winery; do not move a tasting or flight deadline on the assumption that the detour is quick.

For several orders at one winery, ask whether they will be prepared together and how many cartons you should expect. For different wineries, keep a separate confirmation for each. A single total bottle count can hide multiple loading points or a large-format bottle that needs different packing.

Plan the handoff after collection

Tell the ride provider the packed wine load as well as the passengers and ordinary luggage. Ask it to confirm the appropriate vehicle and how the cartons will be secured; no vehicle-class name guarantees case capacity. Vans, Sprinters and buses require a quote.

If you will stop at a hotel before the airport, ask that hotel whether it will accept the cartons, where they will be kept and how you will retrieve them. Do not assume temperature-controlled storage, insurance, overnight vehicle storage or airline-ready packaging is included. Keep the collection receipt and check the order against the winery's handoff while you are there.

Copyable winery request
I plan to visit on [local date]. Could you confirm whether order/release [reference] is ready for collection, its collection deadline, the exact address and available window, and what the attending collector must bring or sign? Please also confirm the packed carton count and whether collection needs a separate appointment from my tasting.

For an existing Koast reservation, send the confirmed collection stops and load to the contact on your confirmation or the agreed day-of-trip contact, and obtain acknowledgment of any route or service change. A new quote does not amend an existing ride. For a new outing, explore Koast wine-country transportation and request a quote with your confirmed stops, party and packed purchases.
